newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's MTRC says funding needs to be small in 1H97.
newsitem.headline: HK's MTRC says funding needs to be small in 1H97.

text.p: Hong Kong's Mass Transit Railway Corp's funding needs will be small in the first half of 1997 and the rest of the year depends on the outlook for new projects, MTRC Treasurer Jimmy Lau said Tuesday.
"Because of the upcoming equity injection, our financing needs in the first half will be very little," Lau said following a seminar at a bond conference here.
The MTRC was eligible for a HK$23.7 billion injection of equity from the government this year for its railway projects related to Hong Kong's new airport, which is under construction.
Lau said the corporation has used HK$19.7 billion of this funding and the remaining HK$4 billion will be used in the first quarter of next year.
Financing needs for all of 1997 will depend on whether the MTRC gets a go-ahead from the government to extend one of its rail lines to Tseung Kwan O, or Junk Bay, he said.
"Then our funding needs would be substantial. Including that project, we would need HK$10 billion per annum over the next few years," said Lau.

The MTRC currently has a HK$3.5 billion revolving credit facility in syndication. The five-year credit pays an all-in return of 41.5 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate, a spread that is more than 20 basis points tighter than the MTRC's previous jumbo loan taken last year.
Lau said the tighter pricing reflects more favorable market conditions this year and the MTRC's strong credit.
Moreover, "Hong Kong banks are still very hungry for non-property assets because so many deals this year have been property related," he said.
The loan already has attracted 12 arrangers and a co-arranger group is being sought, he said.
The MTRC tapped Hong Kong's local bond market with a HK$500 million five-year note issue in August this year.
